use_case: Predictive Maintenance on a Cognitive Digital Twin
how_generated: Each requirement is a triple: (1) an anchor into the knowledge graph, cited by node id - generation aborts if a cited node no longer exists; (2) an IFC probe, which is the only hand-authored part, because ISO 19650 delegates the IFC schema itself to ISO 16739; and (3) a gating level - MANDATORY when the data cannot be joined at all without it, otherwise a weight from 1 to 3. The Pset_Risk property names are not hand-authored either: they are read from the field_* nodes' ifc4_3 / ifc4_0 / ifc2x3 keys, which carry ISO 19650-6 Annex D Table D.2.

normative_basis_for_automated_checking.statement: ISO 19650-4:2022 gives this checker its normative standing: 3.2.3 Note 3 allows an information reviewer to be an artificial intelligence agent or an automated rules-based process; 7.2 makes conformance against the chosen exchange schema a review criterion; 7.6 asks for completeness checks against requirement-derived checklists using repeatable automated processes. An IFC readiness audit under this specification is therefore an information review in the ISO 19650-4 sense, not an extra-standard invention.

sources.definition: presence and adequacy of the information against the level of information need specified by the EIR and any additional expectations. [...] An information reviewer shall consider the following three requirements: to satisfy the purposes associated to the immediate delive

modality_note: Each citation is tagged normative, informative or mixed, straight from the extraction files. ISO 19650-3 Annex A and ISO 19650-5 Annex B are informative: they give 'examples of information that can be required within an AIM', not obligations. ISO 19650-6 Annex C and Annex D are informative too. A requirement whose basis is entirely informative is still sound engineering for this use case, but it is a recommendation of the series rather than a rule of it - M4 is the one mandatory gate in that position.

verdict_rule.cdt_ready: all mandatory pass AND recommended score >= 0.8
verdict_rule.conditional: all mandatory pass AND recommended score >= 0.5, or exactly one mandatory fails with score >= 0.7

requirements.title: Maintainable equipment is modelled as typed distribution elements
requirements.rationale: No typed plant, nothing to maintain: PdM needs pumps, fans, chillers etc. as their IFC classes, not as untyped proxies.

sources.name: asset
sources.definition: item, thing or entity that has potential or actual value to an organization

sources.name: asset and served-system description
sources.definition: descriptions of assets and the asset systems they serve

requirements.if_missing: There is nothing to hang condition data, risks or work orders on. A model full of untyped proxies cannot tell a pump from a handrail, so no asset register can be built from it and the whole loop has no subject.
requirements.probe_human: At least one instance of: IfcPump, IfcFan, IfcCompressor, IfcChiller, IfcBoiler, IfcCoolingTower and 23 more.

requirements.title: Equipment carries stable unique identifiers (GlobalId unique, Name/Tag set)
requirements.rationale: The unique asset identifier is the join key between the IFC model, the H&S register and the condition time series.

sources.definition: unique to the project or asset. [...] Project/asset and originator identifiers can be defined in the project/asset standard methods and procedures.

requirements.if_missing: The IFC model, the health and safety register and the condition time series each end up with their own private key for the same pump. Nothing can be joined, so the sensor reading can never be attributed to the asset it came from.
requirements.probe_human: Every equipment occurrence has a unique GlobalId, and at least 80% of them carry a Name or Tag.

requirements.if_missing: Risk, incident and work-order records cannot resolve a location. Maintenance planning loses access routes and exclusion zones, and a risk cannot be scoped to a zone.
requirements.probe_human: A spatial tree exists (IfcSite, IfcBuilding, IfcBuildingStorey, IfcSpace...) and at least 80% of equipment sits inside it.

requirements.rationale: Annex D maps the H&S context product to IfcSystem, and the asset/served-system description is one of the AIM contents ISO 19650-3 Annex A gives as an example of commercial OIR.

requirements.if_missing: Criticality cannot be reasoned about: you cannot tell that this pump failing takes the whole chilled water loop down, so alert prioritisation degrades to per-component guessing.

requirements.rationale: Categorization shall follow the convention in the project/asset information standard (e.g. Uniclass); classification is how model elements join external code tables in the CDT.

requirements.if_missing: Categorisation has no anchor, so equipment cannot be matched to failure-mode libraries, spares catalogues or the regional risk classification. ISO 19650-6 4.3.7 delegates categorisation to exactly such an external convention.
requirements.probe_human: Equipment is linked to an IfcClassificationReference through IfcRelAssociatesClassification.

requirements.title: Manufacturer and model data on equipment (Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation)
requirements.rationale: ISO 19650-3 Annex A lists vendor data and lead time as example AIM content; manufacturer plus model is the minimum for failure-mode libraries and spares planning.

sources.name: asset vendor data and lead time
sources.definition: vendor data (details of the organization that supplied the asset) including asset lead time

sources.name: spares inventory information
sources.definition: identities and levels of spares held, inter-changeability, specifications and storage locations

requirements.if_missing: Failure modes have to be guessed rather than looked up from the manufacturer's data, and spares and lead time cannot be planned. Pilot can still run on generic models.
requirements.probe_human: At least 50% of equipment carries Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation.

requirements.title: Engineering/design parameters on equipment (Pset_*Common)
requirements.rationale: Design parameters are the reference the condition data is judged against (asset condition and duty).

requirements.if_missing: There is no design duty point to compare a reading against, so anomaly detection has to learn every threshold from scratch instead of starting from the design envelope.
requirements.probe_human: At least 50% of equipment carries a Pset_...Common set.

requirements.title: Condition monitoring points modelled (sensors/instruments/controllers)
requirements.rationale: The sensor is where the condition observation is produced; without modelled monitoring points the twin cannot bind the time series to locations. Also security-relevant: connected plant is Annex B code 41.

requirements.if_missing: The twin has no modelled measurement points, so the time series cannot be bound to a location in the model. Readings can still be attached by asset tag, but the spatial reasoning is lost - and connected plant is also the ISO 19650-5 security surface.
requirements.probe_human: At least one instance of: IfcSensor, IfcSensorType, IfcFlowInstrument, IfcController, IfcControllerType, IfcUnitaryControlElement and 1 more.
